misreadings.quote: whether youthful sensibility draws her toward making the room more terrifying so that only she could enter
misreadings.evidence: "Grete now felt tempted by the desire to make Gregor's situation even more terrifying, so that then she would be able to do even more for him than she had up to now. For surely no one except Grete would ever trust themselves to enter a room in which Gregor ruled the empty walls all by himself."
misreadings.explanation: The narrator gives the purpose of making the room more terrifying as being able to do more for Gregor; that no one else would enter is a separate remark, so presenting exclusivity as the motive goes beyond the text.

result.note: Both versions are otherwise faithful on the furniture expansion after the mother's objection, Grete's hard-won self-confidence, the perhaps/surely shift, and Gregor's unheard decision; only the translation recasts the stated motive as being the only one who could enter.
